reason: Not refuted. VALUE: the case for 0.954 does not assume the successor is better. It rests on tie-defence plus replacing a near-worthless twin. If its copies gain on private, they jump over #37 in a block, and an early verbatim port sits near the top of that block. If they do not gain, the copies stay below us and we lose only the twin, which almost never medals alone: at X it ties late in a block of ~350 copies (rank ~500-650). An independent simplified MC (scratchpad skep_mc.py; notes) reproduces R11S-2. With no successor P(bronze) is 0.72. With a successor, 150 copies and an early port, no action vs port: 0.63 vs 0.80 at mean private gain 0, 0.57 vs 0.83 at +0.4 thousandths, and still 0.68 vs 0.76 at -0.5 (a public-overfit successor). If the successor's private gain is correlated with our insertion's (rho 0.5-0.8), the gain shrinks to +0.02..+0.19, and the worst case is -0.01 (rho 0.8, m -0.5). So acting weakly dominates doing nothing in every run, but R11S-2's '+0.25-0.3' is optimistic. A late port (80% of copies ahead, 300 copies) keeps only +0.04-0.06. NOT A CLOSED LINE: it adds no mechanism of ours. The pre-trigger condition holds: no public notebook is above 0.953 today. HF v3 is at 0.953, anhadmahajan06/biohub-track-your-cells at 0.946 and amanatar at 0.910 (best 0.953), so the threshold is not fitted to a seen notebook. FEASIBILITY: text-only change. tools/e10_port_gate.py has no score threshold (the score is read in the browser, P4c(7)). No pipeline stage, so byte-identity and fail-soft are moot. R8 limits new mechanisms of ours, not the pre-registered port path. The finals #37/#38 are untouched until a trigger. RULE HONESTY: R4 itself maps delta 0 / +0.001 to 'F2 candidate', which is the twin slot, so 0.954 fits R4's letter. It does conflict with P6 ('>= 0.956 = K2 + 0.002; R4'), P4b(c) ('page shows >= 0.956'), §f ('+0.002') and the f2 amendment ('an F2 candidate does not displace the twin'), so the OK text must supersede each of these by name. GAPS: (a) P8 allows ONE port, so a 0.954 port could use it up before a better successor appears. (b) The wording 'at <= 0.953 the copies land at X' is exact only for x138 itself; a new 0.953 notebook's copies land at X+g' with small g'. Doing nothing is still right, but the reason is 'small threat, no signal'. (c) Lowering e10_snapshot's P2 crowd clause (P2_MIN 0.956) to 0.954 would fire on routine x138-variant entrants to the 0.954 block (2 today); keep it at 0.956.
fix: Put the threshold into E10 v2 for the single user OK. In the OK text: (1) Replace '0.956' with '0.954' in P3, P4b(c) and P6. State explicitly that for an E10 port this supersedes P6's R4 '+0.002', §f's '+0.002' and the f2 clause 'an F2 candidate does not displace the twin'. #37 stays in every pair, never {port, #38}. (2) Add a SUPERSEDE clause: a later x138-family successor whose displayed public score is strictly higher than the ported one's (and >= 0.954), and which passes the same gates, replaces the earlier port. At most 2 ports, same last-submit time, same read table. P8's 'ONE port' becomes 'at most two, the second only by this clause'. (3) Reword the <= 0.953 case: 'copies of a new 0.953 notebook land near X; the threat is small and there is no public signal -> notify only'. (4) Keep e10_snapshot P2_MIN at 0.956. A single new public kernel at >= 0.954 is already a P2 look signal through dateRun/scoreDescending; R11S-7's flag is optional. (5) Keep the 3-hourly checks from 27 Sep 12:00 to 29 Sep 06:00 UTC (R11S-6), since the port's value depends on submitting early inside the copy block. (6) Present the numbers as priors: conditional on a trigger, +0.02..+0.26 P(bronze) (correlation-dependent, worst case -0.01); unconditional increment over the in-force 0.956 rule ~+0.005-0.015. Until the OK, the 0.956 rule stays in force.
realistic_gain: Conditional on a public x138-family successor at 0.954-0.955 that passes the gates and is ported early: about +0.02 to +0.26 P(bronze) over doing nothing (central ~+0.1-0.2; worst modelled case -0.01). The chance of that band triggering by 29 Sep 06:00 UTC is ~5%, so the unconditional gain over the current 0.956 rule is ~+0.005-0.015 P(bronze). In the ~90% no-trigger world it changes nothing, at the cost of a text edit and one user OK.
